articles.title: More Americans believe the government is withholding information about UFOs
articles.summary: The truth may be out there, but Americans are split on what the truth is: just under half of people believe all sightings of unidentified flying object (UFO), also known as unidentified anomalous phenomena (UAP), can be explained by human activity or natural phenomena, a new Gallup poll finds. The proportion of skeptics has been dropping, however: In 2019, 60 percent of Americans said they believed UAP were either human-caused or natural phenomena. That’s not to say that all those with shifting opinions are sure our planet has been visited by intelligent life from other planets: 37 percent of the poll’s respondents said some UAP were likely alien spacecraft, down from 41 percent in 2021.

articles.title: Exclusive: Brussels keen to monitor UFOs under the radar
articles.summary: Brussels has signalled it is monitoring unidentified anomalous phenomena (UAP) and has hinted at improving capabilities, according to documents seen by Euronews. The European Commission seems to have been monitoring unidentified anomalous phenomena (UAP) under the radar since at least 2023, according to a document from the Commission's defence department seen by Euronews, which pertains to sky and space observations in Malaysia. "We are getting better at seeing it (UAPs) and better identifying it as our technological capacities improve, but we need to get even better," the letter read, signalling the EU executive is actively monitoring the phenomenon more than officially stated and seems keen to investigate it.

de.title: Exklusiv: Brüssel will UFOs unter dem Radar überwachen
de.summary: Laut Euronews-Dokumenten hat Brüssel signalisiert, dass es nicht identifizierte anomale Phänomene (UAP) überwacht, und angedeutet, seine Fähigkeiten zu verbessern. Laut einem von Euronews eingesehenen Dokument der Verteidigungsabteilung der Kommission, das sich auf Himmels- und Weltraumbeobachtungen in Malaysia bezieht, scheint die Europäische Kommission seit mindestens 2023 unidentifizierte anomale Phänomene (UAP) unter dem Radar zu überwachen. „Wir werden immer besser darin, es zu sehen (UAPs) und es besser zu identifizieren, während sich unsere technologischen Kapazitäten verbessern, aber wir müssen noch besser werden“, heißt es in dem Brief und signalisiert damit, dass die EU-Exekutive das Phänomen aktiver beobachtet als offiziell angegeben und offenbar daran interessiert zu sein scheint, es zu untersuchen.

articles.summary: More New Jersey UFO reports keep pouring in When New Jersey residents look up to the skies over the Garden State, some of them are seeing more than birds, planes, and SpaceX launches. Not every light or shape in the New Jersey sky is a UFO, or as they are known these days, UAP, but some of the things we are seeing are not easily explained. There is a website that keeps track of reported sightings, and it's called the National UFO Reporting Center. articles.title: Pilots report ‘unexplained lights’ over Cyprus as EU monitors UFO reports
articles.summary: Pilots have reported unexplained aerial phenomena (UAPs) over Cyprus, including a sighting involving six crew members on a flight south of the island. As reported by Euronews, the Cyprus incident was described by Dutch airline pilot Rob Ackermans, who said he and five other crew members observed unusual lights for more than two hours during a flight from the Middle East to the Netherlands in 2023. Ackermans said the phenomenon first appeared while the aircraft was south of Cyprus. “The strangest thing was that one of the three lights would sometimes manoeuvre around the others. It looked like a chase, what the air force calls a dogfight, and then two or all three would disappear again.
